# POS App
> A modern, high-performance Point of Sale system.

## Tech Stack
- PHP 8.4 + Laravel 13
- React 19 + TypeScript 5
- Inertia.js v3
- Tailwind CSS v4
- Pest 4 (Testing)

## Core Directories & Files
- [app/]: Laravel backend core (Controllers, Models, Actions, Policies).
- [routes/]: Application routing (web, api).
- [resources/js/]: Frontend React application (Inertia setup).
- [resources/js/pages/]: React page components (mapped to routes).
- [resources/js/components/]: Reusable UI components (shadcn/ui based).
- [resources/js/types/]: TypeScript definitions and strict frontend contracts.
- [docs/]: General documentation and Architecture Decision Records (ADRs).

## Key Concepts
- **Inertia.js Routing**: The frontend is a React monolith acting as a SPA, but routing is driven by Laravel. Use `router.visit()` or `<Link>` from `@inertiajs/react`.
- **POS Architecture**: The core checkout loop relies on React local state for cart management and communicates with Laravel for final transaction processing.
- **Strict Typing**: The project enforces strict TypeScript guidelines on the frontend and strong PHP typing (Larastan) on the backend.
- **Tailwind v4**: Styling is utility-first, using the latest Tailwind CSS version. Custom components often wrap `lucide-react` for iconography.
- **Permissions**: Spatie Laravel Permission is used on the backend and injected into the frontend `auth.roles` props to conditionally render UI elements.

## AI Assistant Guidelines
- Before generating code, check the `resources/js/types` for existing interfaces.
- Use `isNavLeaf(item)` type guard when handling navigation items.
- Avoid introducing inline `setState` in `useEffect` synchronously; derive state or use `useLayoutEffect` where appropriate to prevent cascading renders.
- Run `npm run lint` and `npm run types:check` to ensure frontend quality after major edits.
- Exclude `.agents/`, `.claude/`, and `.opencode/` scripts when analyzing project source code for linting or refactoring.
